# Test change conventions

These comma-separated path/name patterns are only an initial match. They do not cover every language or project naming scheme, and they do not prescribe code or test directories. Extend `applyTo` to fit the real project when adopting it; **read these rules explicitly whenever you modify any test, even if automatic matching did not trigger.**

- Keep the project's actual test layout and existing style. First read the target acceptance criteria, the corresponding VT, and [verify-change](../skills/verify-change/SKILL.md), and check gaps across the full scope instead of picking only existing tests.
- Tests map to specific behaviors, boundaries, and forbidden side effects, and use full acceptance IDs. When requirements change, re-review the source and expected outcome first; do not hide differences by changing assertions or deleting targets.
- Commands, tools, environment, and cwd follow the [actual development registration](../../docs/development.md#project-registration) and the actual project; do not assume a runner or invent build/test commands.
- Record only actual runs and per-item evidence; zero discoveries, all-skipped, or a zero exit code alone cannot prove that acceptance passed. When the object or environment is missing, write `not-run` with the reason; document checks do not replace business or software runs.
- Regression tests for the maintenance tools keep positive and negative subprocess cases that use real files, local Git objects, and the current interpreter, with argument lists, an explicit cwd, and `shell=False`. Do not mock Git stdout, and do not compute expected identities, counts, or states from the implementation under test. Inject an explicit I/O boundary only where an OS failure cannot be produced safely, and distinguish actually observed results from injected ones.
- Fixtures use the standard temporary directory and must not require a fixed `.venv` under the checkout or the interpreter installation directory to be writable; resolve the canonical path of the temporary directory on the host. Generic script behavior must run in CI on Windows, Linux, and macOS; separate cases only for genuinely platform-specific adaptation details, and do not hide missing functionality by skipping whole categories. CLIs should be launchable from another cwd and cover spaces, non-ASCII (for example CJK) paths, and non-default environment locations.
- The `checked_count/attempted_count` of the [formal artifact check](../utilities/README.md#artifact-checker) are not test discovered/executed/skipped counts. Regression records must list runner counts separately and reject a "success" with zero discoveries or all tests skipped; compare the raw bytes of inputs before and after the check, and list report output separately. Maker-repository tests are not distributed with downstream candidates and are not a prerequisite for running the downstream checker.
